summary_rationale: Garware Hi-Tech Films has structurally transformed from a 7–10% OPM commodity BOPET producer (FY15–FY18) into an 86% value-added specialty films franchise (73–75% Consumer Products: Sun Control, Architectural, and Paint Protection Films) generating 21%–28.7% operating margins, 10 consecutive years of positive Free Cash Flow, zero long-term debt (ICRA AA Stable / CARE AA- Stable), seven straight years of unqualified audits, and ₹933 crore in cash and liquid investments as of September 2026. Chip-to-film vertical integration and the Q3 FY2027 Lubrizol-partnered TPU extrusion line provide a durable cost moat (54–60% gross margins vs. ~42–45% for asset-light peer XPEL). KPI health remains PASS_WITH_WATCH due to high US geographic concentration (45–51% of sales), ~30% single-customer concentration, elevated FY26 inventory days (149 days), unnotified Finance Ministry enactment of DGTR's June 2026 anti-dumping recommendation on Chinese TPU PPF (where DGTR documented <25% total domestic volume share and CY24 domestic PPF losses under 200%–300% undercutting), India CMVR Rule 100 automotive tint enforcement friction, component-auditor reliance on foreign subsidiaries (~36% of FY26 revenue), and ₹215.74 crore in contingent liabilities/commitments including an unprovided ₹18.37 crore disputed tax demand.
